name: What is the difference between a tankless and a traditional hot water heater?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tankless and a traditional hot water heater?

acceptedAnswer.text: A traditional hot water heater stores and heats a large tank of water constantly, providing a limited supply of hot water at a time. Once the tank is depleted, you must wait for it to refill and reheat. Tankless water heaters, conversely, heat water on demand as it flows through the unit, providing a continuous supply of hot water. Tankless systems are generally more energy-efficient and take up less space, but have a higher upfront cost and may require gas line or electrical upgrades.
acceptedAnswer.description: Traditional heaters store and constantly heat water in a tank. Tankless heaters heat water on demand, offering continuous hot water and higher efficiency.
